title: Multimodal Labeling
subtitle: Text, images and audio, with review built in
description: A Rust + React labeling platform with configurable schemas, multi-annotator agreement and optional model-assisted pre-labeling. One Docker image to self-host.
longDescription: A Rust + React labeling platform with configurable schemas, multi-annotator agreement and optional model-assisted pre-labeling. One Docker image to self-host. Rewritten from the original Flask application in 2026, keeping annotation, review and export in one workspace.
mascotLines: The 2B model is over 90% sure about almost everything. A person still presses the key.
imageCaptions: Labelling a sentence: score, sentiment and type, next to the model's suggestion and reason
Image plus text, in dark mode; the model rates the cat picture a match for the crime
Progress and agreement: coverage, counts per annotator, Krippendorff's alpha and kappas
Optional login: accounts as annotator, reviewer or admin, with password resets
features: Configurable schemas for text, image and audio classification
Optional model-assisted pre-labeling and built-in login
results: 2026 Rust and React rewrite with import, annotation, review and export
why: The models at my first job needed labelled sentences, and the 2019 Flask version, emoLabel, scored the emotion in each one. The 2026 rewrite lets a model suggest labels first. A 2B model is 90 to 100% sure of nearly every answer, so a person still presses the key.
gains: For turning text, images or audio into training or evaluation data: one self-hosted Docker image, a schema per project, keyboard labelling, and kappa scores showing whether people and the model agree. The chat export shares the prompt, so a model tuned on it can return as the one making suggestions.
lessons: Thinking models used up Ollama's default 4,096-token context and got cut off mid-answer; the -instruct model or an 8,192 context fixed it.
The old database declared text as INTEGER, so SQLite stored a text like '2019' as a number; the importer casts it back.
Batch pre-labelling hit 'database is locked' because deferred transactions don't wait for the lock; BEGIN IMMEDIATE fixed it.
